newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU stock data expected to confirm gasoil tightness.
newsitem.headline: EU stock data expected to confirm gasoil tightness.

text.p: Traders are expected to focus a little more than usual on EU stock figures due out on Wednesday, figures which are likely to demonstrate the tightness of gas oil supply in Europe, analysts and trader say.
"Normally (the Euroilstocks report) would not be that important, but there should be attention this time as Europe is in the driving seat," said Peter Bogin of Cambridge Energy Research Associates.

Analysts and traders differ as to whether European primary stocks will have grown or declined in September, but few expect dramatic movement either way which will mean that stock levels at the beginning of October were historically low.
"It will mean it's rather tight. It should support prices and provide scope for a potential (price) hike if the weather turns cold," one trader said.

IPE gas oil futures reached their highest level since January 1991, $250.00 a tonne, on Friday last week and again on Monday. Traders and analysts say European gas oil holds the key to the strength of the oil complex and have prompted a cargo volume estimated at about 570,000 tonnes to come from the United States this month.
Geoff Pyne, analyst at UBS, expects a modest build of stocks, but believes the outlook for prices, influenced by gas oil, will be firm.

"Normally, primary stocks increase in the third quarter by about a million barrels per day. This year, we've managed about 0.7 million a day and from a low start. The near term outlook for prices should therefore be firm," Pyne said.
Pyne adds that stocks were drawn down ahead of the expected resumption of limited Iraqi exports which failed to materialise.
"Now they have extra low stocks and no Iraq, although in the latter half of the month, (majors) have had the chance to build stocks up," Pyne said.
Traders say German end user demand for gas oil was high in September, although cargoes from the U.S. and the former Soviet Union have compensated at least in part.
Peter Bogin expects EU September gas oil stocks to be stable or slightly down, given flows to Germany.
"It should add support to the market, despite the figures from the U.S. yesterday," Bogin said.

A report by the American Petroleum Institute said distillate stocks in the United States had risen by 1.3 million barrels to 113.6 million in the week ending October 4. This was 17.1 million barrels lower than in the equivalent week last year.

The Euroilstock Foundation figures are due out at 1300 GMT. In August, middle distillate stocks rose 3.75 million barrels to 286.28 million, against 312.07 million in August 1995. In September last year, middle distillate stocks stood at 309.15 million barrels.
